scope: Colony and biological-image methods relevant to CountScope's large/faint colony misses and scale tradeoffs
readingBasis: Focused reading of publisher article text, methods/results excerpts, author repositories and official documentation. Publisher PDF endpoints were checked but the web reader hit cookie redirects; no local PDF downloads are claimed.
venuePolicy: Nature Methods papers are the top-journal core. ICIP is a conference. Scientific Reports is an application-journal supplement, not interchangeable with Nature or Nature Methods. No journal impact-factor or ranking claims are made.

papers.title: Cellpose 2.0: how to train your own model
papers.dataDomain: Cellular microscopy; TissueNet, LiveCell and Cellpose instance-mask datasets
papers.keyIdea: Different annotation styles and image domains can require different models; targeted human-in-the-loop corrections can adapt a pretrained segmenter efficiently.
papers.relevance: Audit whether large diffuse colonies and small sharp colonies have consistent object/boundary definitions, and balance morphology coverage instead of relying on object-weighted aggregate scores.
papers.currentDataFit: Our boxes allow detection/count checks, but supervised Cellpose training needs genuine instance masks. Filled rectangles are not substitute mask ground truth.
papers.doNotClaim: Its small annotation-budget results on specific microscopy datasets do not guarantee equivalent CFU performance or labeling effort.
papers.proposedUse: After a small zero-shot probe, curate training-only masks for underrepresented morphology groups and refine a pretrained model; keep validation/test labels independent.

papers.title: Cellpose3: one-click image restoration for improved cellular segmentation
papers.dataDomain: Noisy, blurry and undersampled microscopy images; diverse cellular/nuclear datasets
papers.keyIdea: Train restoration for a downstream segmentation objective with perceptual similarity, rather than optimizing pixel reconstruction alone.
papers.relevance: Useful hypothesis for faint boundaries, but apparent image sharpening is not evidence of correct colony counts.
papers.currentDataFit: Pretrained restoration can be tested without new labels. Reproducing its training needs appropriate masks and reference images; current boxes cannot establish mask quality.
papers.doNotClaim: The paper's microscopy results and hallucination analysis do not prove safe restoration or accurate CFU separation on RGB agar photographs.
papers.proposedUse: Compare raw input against one conservative pretrained-restoration branch on validation; measure extra false positives as well as rescued true positives. Preserve original pixels and provenance.

papers.title: Omnipose: a high-precision morphology-independent solution for bacterial cell segmentation
papers.dataDomain: Individual bacterial cells in phase-contrast/fluorescence microscopy; elongated and branched morphologies
papers.keyIdea: A distance-field-gradient representation improves segmentation across difficult cell shapes.
papers.relevance: Supports treating morphology variation as a representation/data problem, not simply increasing tile count.
papers.currentDataFit: Mask-based training would require new verified instance masks. A pretrained probe can be scored as counts/boxes, but not as mask AP with our existing labels.
papers.doNotClaim: A microscopic bacterial cell is not a macroscopic colony-forming unit; directly counting its predicted masks on a plate may count texture within a colony.
papers.proposedUse: Consider only after morphology-balanced mask annotation or a bounded validation probe; do not assume the bacterial preset is already a colony counter.

papers.title: CellSAM: a foundation model for cell segmentation
papers.dataDomain: Mammalian cells, yeast and bacteria across cellular imaging modalities
papers.keyIdea: CellFinder automatically proposes object boxes that prompt SAM to produce instance masks.
papers.relevance: Architecture matches the desire for automatic proposal/region selection and offers a route to training-mask assistance.
papers.currentDataFit: Existing TRAIN boxes can prompt candidate masks for correction. Feeding TEST truth boxes would already supply object locations/counts and cannot demonstrate automatic counting.
papers.doNotClaim: CellSAM has not been demonstrated here on agar colonies or on-device. Its published full training used multiple A100 GPUs; local full replication is inappropriate.
papers.proposedUse: Optional pretrained CPU probe or training-only annotation teacher. Official inspected API documents CPU/CUDA, not an established MPS path.

papers.title: Slicing Aided Hyper Inference and Fine-Tuning for Small Object Detection
papers.venue: IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP)
papers.publicationType: peer-reviewed conference paper; not a journal
papers.dataDomain: Small aerial objects in VisDrone and xView
papers.keyIdea: Preserve small-object resolution with overlapping slices and merge predictions; official implementation also retains a full-image pass for large targets.
papers.relevance: Current four-tile-only policy loses large-colony recall. The missing whole-image branch is directly testable with existing predictions and labels.
papers.currentDataFit: Directly compatible with bounding-box/count annotations; no new masks or detector retraining required for the first ablation.
papers.doNotClaim: Reported aerial AP gains are not colony counting accuracy. Aggressive IoS/NMM merging can combine distinct adjacent colonies.
papers.proposedUse: Compare conservative full+tile IoU fusion and a limited scale-gated variant against both baselines; select on validation with count, TP/FP/FN and size/species gates.

papers.title: Overcoming resolution constraints in automated colony counting via a high-performance deep learning framework using SAHI
papers.publicationType: peer-reviewed application journal article; supporting domain evidence, not Nature Methods/Nature
papers.codeStatus: No article-specific repository was verified; upstream SAHI is available.
papers.dataDomain: The same public 24-species colony dataset family used in our experiment
papers.keyIdea: Native-resolution640px tiles with20percent overlap for training/inference outperform aggressively resized plates in the authors' experiment.
papers.relevance: Supports scale preservation and train/inference scale consistency, but does not directly solve our large diffuse morphologies.
papers.currentDataFit: Uses boxes. Any derived crops must remain grouped with their source physical plate before splitting.
papers.doNotClaim: Their24-class original-image split and our unseen-species single-class split differ. Their reported96.9percent mAP is not a CountScope replication or count-correctness target.
papers.proposedUse: Use as a secondary scale-training ablation reference, retaining full-plate exposure and checking per-morphology counts rather than copying its headline score.

notCountedAsVerifiedTopJournal.title: Cellpose-SAM: superhuman generalization for cellular segmentation
notCountedAsVerifiedTopJournal.status: The official Cellpose repository still cites a bioRxiv paper; no journal version was verified in this pass. Do not confuse it with CellSAM, the Nature Methods2025 paper.

localFeasibility.hardwareContext: M5 Pro,24GB from parent; no timing or memory benchmark was run by this reviewer
localFeasibility.firstChoice: Existing-detector whole+tile fusion: reuse cached predictions or current lightweight model; avoid another large training job until ablation evidence exists.
localFeasibility.cellpose3: Official3.1.1.1 docs expose an MPS option. Version3.1.1 release notes route mask postprocessing to CPU on Mac and use float32 in a flow step. Pin an isolated environment and verify CPU/MPS outputs before a batch.
localFeasibility.omnipose: Current official2.0 README advertises MPS and tests Python3.10-3.12; the existing training environment is Python3.9, so do not silently upgrade it in place.
localFeasibility.cellsam: Full paper training is beyond this workstation plan. Pretrained CPU inference may be probed, but neither MPS nor iPhone/CoreML performance is established.

proposedExperimentOrder.hypothesis: Full-image detections recover large targets that the fixed crop-only policy drops.
proposedExperimentOrder.action: Pre-register a small full+tile fusion ablation with a conservative IoU merger and one scale-aware candidate. Tune only on validation. Keep original whole and four-tile outputs for exact comparison.
proposedExperimentOrder.gate: Require countMAE improvement plus no material TP regression, inspect FP/FN by size and species, and report macro-species metrics alongside micro totals.

proposedExperimentOrder.hypothesis: Canonical-scale segmentation or task-aware restoration could recover low-contrast boundaries.
proposedExperimentOrder.action: Bounded pretrained Cellpose3 probe on representative validation images at training-derived size settings; optionally compare raw and restored input. Do not use test truth boxes to guide inference.
proposedExperimentOrder.gate: Available labels support count/box checks only; mask quality needs new audited masks. Reject extra false cells and split colonies, even if images look cleaner.

proposedExperimentOrder.hypothesis: Data diversity and annotation-style consistency matter more than repeating the same dominant morphology.
proposedExperimentOrder.action: Create a small training-only, morphology-balanced mask set through proposal-and-correction, explicitly defining diffuse edges and touching-colony treatment. Then fine-tune a suitable small segmentation model.
proposedExperimentOrder.gate: Use genuinely new acquisition groups for final evaluation; do not rewrite historical test labels or present the already-open63-image set as fresh blind validation.
proposedExperimentOrder.cost: Requires new segmentation supervision; no such labels were produced here.

importantNonClaims: Microscopic single-cell segmentation is not automatically macroscopic colony counting.
A high micro AP score dominated by one phenotype cannot establish general-colony reliability.
Paper metrics from other splits, classes, imaging systems and hardware are not our measured accuracy or speed.
Old63-image test results can be regression evidence after method development, but not a newly independent test.
No App Store, production model, training dataset or dependency environment was changed by this research lane.
